question: Clacton by-election: Count Binface Vote %
resolution_criteria:
A by-election for the United Kingdom parliamentary constituency of Clacton is expected to be held soon following the announced resignation of incumbent Nigel Farage.

This market will resolve according to the share of valid votes Count Binface wins in the Clacton parliamentary by-election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If the specified candidate does not compete or the results of the specified election are not known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting. In case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official election results as published by Tendring District Council (https://www.tendringdc.gov.uk/) and the UK Parliament (https://www.parliament.uk/).
research:
**Clacton by-election: Count Binface vote share. Research using only sources dated on or before 2026-08-04**

Several search results reported events after 2026-08-04. I left them out, as instructed.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07 (date not shown): Tendring District Council runs a page for the "13 August 2026 - Election of Member of Parliament to the Clacton Constituency". It posted the Statement of Persons Nominated and Notice of Poll as a PDF. Up to 2026-08-04 there were no results, because voting hadn't happened yet. I did not open the PDF. [Tendring DC](https://www.tendringdc.gov.uk/content/13-august-2026-election-of-member-of-parliament-to-the-clacton-constituency), [SOPN PDF](https://legacy.tendringdc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/council/elections%20&%20voting/2026/Aug13/UKPGE%20-%20NOP%20SOP%20SOPN.pdf)
- The UK Parliament election results site has a page for this by-election. [parliament.uk](https://electionresults.parliament.uk/elections/4556)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-08-04, nothing has settled the question. Polling day is 13 August 2026 and the count follows overnight.
- 2026-07-17: Binface is on the ballot. Nominations are confirmed, with a record 34 candidates. [Nation.Cymru/PA](https://nation.cymru/news/nigel-farage-one-of-34-candidates-in-clacton-by-election/), [Gazette](https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/26291497.34-candidates-clacton-by-election/)
- Labour, the Conservatives, the Lib Dems, the Greens and Restore Britain are all standing aside. That leaves Binface as the main anti-Farage option. Laurence Fox (Reclaim), Monster Raving Loony candidates and many independents are also standing. [freebets.com](https://www.freebets.com/news/clacton-by-election-odds-count-binface-odds-slashed-as-main-parties-stand-aside/), [OLBG](https://www.olbg.com/news/clacton-election-odds-reform-slashed-1-20-34-candidate-field-confirmed-no-main-westminster-rivals-standing)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-03: The London Economic reported the first constituency poll, by Survation for Mandate Research (first carried by The Times on 2 August):
  - Full field: Farage about 73%, Binface about 20%, all others about 7%.
  - Head-to-head: Farage 69%, Binface 31%.
  - Another search summary put the sample at 502 adults, but the article itself gave no sample size or fieldwork dates. [TLE](https://www.thelondoneconomic.com/politics/clacton-by-election-poll-count-binface-nigel-farage-408423/)
- 2026-08-03: Oddschecker reportedly had Farage at 1/20 and Binface out to 25/1 (SpreadEX) to win. The page blocked fetching, so I only have this from the search summary. [Oddschecker](https://www.oddschecker.com/insight/politics/20260803-clacton-by-election-odds-favourites-candidates-when-is-the-election)
- 2026-07-21: RTÉ ran "Could Count Binface actually beat Nigel Farage?" It cited a national Ipsos poll:
  - 33% of Britons would prefer Binface to win, against 21% for Farage.
  - 54% said Farage should have resigned.
  - 74% want the standards investigation to continue.
  - Note that this measures national preference, not Clacton voting intention. [RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2026/0721/1584151-nigel-farage-reform-uk-count-binface-clacton-bye-election-2026/), [Ipsos](https://www.ipsos.com/en-uk/british-public-more-likely-prefer-count-binface-wins-clacton-election-nigel-farage)
- 2026-07-10: The poll date of 13 August was confirmed. [ITV](https://www.itv.com/news/anglia/2026-07-10/date-confirmed-for-clacton-by-election-after-farage-mp-resignation)
- 2026-07-08: William Hill had Binface at 7/2 and Reform at 1/6. Binface is presenting himself as an anti-Farage "unity candidate". [William Hill](https://news.williamhill.com/politics/count-binface-clacton/), [freebets.com](https://www.freebets.com/news/clacton-by-election-odds-count-binface-odds-slashed-as-main-parties-stand-aside/)
- 2026-07-07: Farage resigned his seat. Critics link the resignation to a standards probe over an undeclared £5m gift from Christopher Harborne. [RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2026/0721/1584151-nigel-farage-reform-uk-count-binface-clacton-bye-election-2026/)

## 4. Base rates
- Binface's past results are tiny: a few hundred votes at most, with a best of about 308 votes in a parliamentary contest.
- 2026-06-18: In the Makerfield by-election he got 95 votes (0.2%) and finished 7th. [parliament.uk](https://electionresults.parliament.uk/elections/4555)
- Those contests are poor comparisons, because the main parties were standing in all of them. When major parties stand aside, the closest precedent is a single serious challenger soaking up the opposition vote.
- Clacton context: in 2024 Reform won with about 46%. The rest of the vote was split among the Conservatives, Labour, the Lib Dems and the Greens. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clacton_in_the_2024_United_Kingdom_general_election)
- Turnout is likely to be low, and some anti-Farage voters may abstain or spoil their ballots. Spoilt ballots are not counted as valid votes. This is my own observation, not a sourced figure.

## 5. Other forecasts
- The Survation constituency poll (reported 2026-08-02/03) put Binface at about 20%. That sits right on the line between the 10-20% and 20-30% brackets. A figure of exactly 20% would resolve to the higher bracket.
- Bookmaker vote-share bands (OLBG). The article page shows "updated 2 September", so the date these odds were captured is uncertain. They appear to be pre-poll prices:

  | Market | Odds |
  |---|---|
  | Over 22.5% | 10/11 |
  | Under 22.5% | 4/5 |
  | 5-9.99% | 9/2 |
  | 10-14.99% | 6/1 |
  | 15-19.99% | 5/1 |
  | 20-24.99% | 7/2 |
  | 25-29.99% | 6/1 |
  | 30-34.99% | 7/1 |

  Binface to win had drifted from 9/2 to 8/1. [OLBG](https://www.olbg.com/news/clacton-election-odds-reform-slashed-1-20-34-candidate-field-confirmed-no-main-westminster-rivals-standing)
- Polymarket "Count Binface Vote %":
  - A July snapshot reported by Lines put "<10%" at about 28.5%.
  - Another snapshot (undated) had "<10%" as the top bracket at about 35%.
  - I could not get prices as of 2026-08-04 (Lines returned 403). [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/politics/clacton-by-election-count-binface-vote-20260708142507718), [polymarkets mirror](https://polymarkets.co.il/en/market/clacton-by-election-count-binface-vote-20260708142507718/)
- Vote-Scope's model gave Binface roughly a 1-4% chance of winning; I did not find a vote-share estimate there. [Vote-Scope](https://vote-scope.com/en/uk/byelections/clacton/)
- Manifold has related markets, such as Binface over or under 25%. I did not get their prices. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Fastcar99/will-count-binface-get-under-or-ove)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More constituency polls, and any tactical-voting endorsements of Binface, for example from local Labour, Lib Dem or Green figures. The anti-Farage tactical campaign is the key variable.
- Developments in the standards investigation into Farage.
- Polling day on 2026-08-13, with the count and declaration overnight into 2026-08-14. Results are then published by Tendring DC and Parliament.
- Turnout and the number of spoilt ballots. Spoilt ballots are excluded from the valid-vote denominator, so they change Binface's share.

**Reasoning:** I am centring on about 18-24%, with roughly equal weight on 10-20% and 20-30%. A result of exactly 20% would resolve to the higher bracket. I keep meaningful tails on both sides.

trongest evidence:
* Survation poll for Mandate Research, reported in The Times on 2 August 2026: Farage 73%, Binface 20%, others 7%; head-to-head 69% to 31%.
* Bookmaker vote-share bands: over/under 22.5% priced at roughly evens. After removing the overround, they imply about 20% for under 10%, about 28% for 10-20%, about 32% for 20-30% and about 18% for 30% and above.
* Labour, the Conservatives, the Lib Dems, the Greens and Restore Britain are all standing aside (confirmed 17 July), leaving Binface as the main anti-Farage option.
* Binface to win drifted out to 8/1 and then 25/1, which suggests a share of around 20-30% rather than one challenging Farage.
* Earlier Polymarket snapshots in July favoured under 10% at about 28-35%. These came before the poll, so I give them less weight.

(e) Unexpected outcomes:
* Low (under 10%): anti-Farage voters stay home or spoil their ballots, and the 34-candidate field (Fox, the Loonies, many independents) splits the protest vote.
* High (30% or more): tactical endorsements and anger over the standards investigation consolidate the opposition vote behind Binface, close to the 31% head-to-head figure, especially if Reform turnout is complacent.

Weighting: I move from the bookmaker-implied distribution toward the poll, so less weight on under 10% and a centre around 20-24%, while keeping wide tails because there is only one constituency poll of uncertain quality.

Option_B: 0.31
